data.title: FAA set to approve Boeing 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • FAA completed key Type Certification Board safety review on Friday, sources say
  • Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, about 30% of 737 backlog
  • FAA said October 2 navigation software glitch posed no safety concern

By David Shepardson and Dan Catchpole

The Federal Aviation Administration is set to approve the long-delayed Boeing 737 MAX 10 as soon as next week, after completing a key safety review on Friday, three people familiar with the matter said.

The review by the Type Certification Board — made up of FAA management team members — is a final step before the agency decides on certification. The MAX 10 is a larger variant of Boeing's best-selling 737 MAX and its expected approval marks a key milestone for the US planemaker.

Boeing has faced a more stringent certification process since two fatal MAX 8 crashes in 2018 and 2019, as well as scrutiny of the company's production and quality systems after a January 2024 mid-air cabin panel blowout on a nearly new Alaska Airlines MAX 9.

Asked for comment, the FAA said, "Safety dictates the certification timeline." Boeing referred questions to the FAA.

The FAA in August gave long-awaited ​approval to the smaller 737 MAX 7 after reviewing the plane for more than eight years. Boeing at one point planned to start delivering the MAX 10 in 2020.

A problem with the anti-ice system on 737 MAX engines that arose in 2023 further delayed certification of the MAX 7 and 10.

The delays have helped European rival Airbus' A321neo secure a greater share of the large single-aisle market. Boeing has said the MAX 10 will be a major cash-flow driver in its ongoing financial recovery following years of crises and controversies.

Airlines have ordered nearly 1,500 MAX 10s, and the model accounts for about 30% of Boeing's outstanding 737 backlog. The planemaker has already built a handful of MAX 10s awaiting delivery.

The bigger plane that can carry more passengers is crucial to several airlines' growth plans. Major customers for the MAX 10 include United Airlines , Alaska, Ryanair , Delta Air Lines and American Airlines .

A glitch with the latest update of the 737 MAX's navigation software threatened to further delay certification when Boeing disclosed it in late September. However, the FAA determined on October 2 that it did not pose a safety concern and did not require Boeing to fix the problem as a condition of certifying the plane.

Boeing is still working on certifying the 777-9, its largest jetliner in production, which is already six years behind schedule. The company has said it expects to complete certification and begin deliveries in 2027.

data.title: US natural gas prices fall 4% on mild weather and lower demand view
data.description:
Key points:
  • Output eased from August-September records after storm-related shut-ins and pipeline disruptions
  • Golden Pass feedgas hit a record 0.7 bcfd; Sabine Pass reached four-month high
  • European and Asian benchmarks climbed near $29 per mmBtu

By Scott DiSavino

US natural gas futures fell about 4% to a one-week low on Friday on continued mild weather, lowered demand forecasts and a small increase in output in recent days.

Front-month gas futures for November delivery on the New York Mercantile Exchange fell 12 cents, or 4%, to settle at $3.116 per million British thermal units (mmBtu), their lowest close since October 6.

That also put the contract down about 3% this week after it gained about 6% last week.

Financial firm LSEG said average gas output in the US Lower 48 states slid from record highs of 113.3 bcfd in August and September to 110.8 bcfd so far in October. The average so far in October was slightly higher than on Thursday.

That drop in output so far in October was due to a combination of Gulf of Mexico shut-ins from Hurricane Isaias and force majeure incidents and other problems on pipelines in Kentucky, Texas, West Virginia and elsewhere in recent weeks.

With seasonally colder weather coming, LSEG said average gas demand in the Lower 48 states, including exports, will rise from 103.87 bcfd this week to 106.8 bcfd over the next two weeks. The forecast for this week was lower than LSEG's outlook on Thursday, while the forecast for next week was higher.

LNG EXPORTS

Average gas flows to the nine major US LNG export plants slid to 17.6 bcfd so far in October, down from 17.9 bcfd in September and a monthly record high of 18.8 bcfd in April.

On a daily basis, LNG export feedgas was on track to rise to a five-month high of 18.9 bcfd on Friday with flows to Cheniere Energy's 4.5-bcfd Sabine Pass plant in Louisiana at a four-month high of 4.8 bcfd and flows to the first 0.8-bcfd liquefaction train at ExxonMobil /QatarEnergy's Golden Pass plant in Texas up to a record 0.7 bcfd.

LNG export plants often pull in more gas than they can turn into LNG since they use some of that gas to fuel liquefaction and other equipment.

Around the world, gas traded at both the Dutch Title Transfer Facility benchmark in Europe and the Japan-Korea Marker (JKMc1) benchmark in Asia.

Global gas prices have spiked in recent years primarily due to supply disruptions linked to Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and the US-Israeli war with Iran this year.

Prices in the US, however, have not reacted much to the war in Iran because the US produces all the gas it consumes domestically and US LNG companies are already liquefying as much fuel as they can.

No matter how high global gas prices go, the US cannot export much more LNG until units under construction enter service in coming months and years.

data.title: Malaga Financial Corporation Reports Record Earnings for the Third Quarter and First Nine Months of 2026
data.description:
PALOS VERDES ESTATES, Calif., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Malaga Financial Corporation “Company” OTCIQ:MLGF, the parent company of Malaga Bank FSB, today reported that net income for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 was $18,028,000 ($1.82 basic and fully diluted earnings per share) compared to $16,431,000 ($1.66 basic and fully diluted earnings per share, as adjusted for the stock dividend declared on November 14, 2025) for the same period ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $1,597,000 or 10%. For the first nine months of 2026, the Company’s annualized return on average equity was 10.52% and the annualized return on average assets was 1.66%.

The $1,597,000 increase in year-to-date net income was primarily due to $2,631,000 increase in net interest income after provision for loan losses, a $307,000 identity fraud recovery, partially offset by $622,000 increase in other operating expenses and $670,000 increase in income taxes.

Net income for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, was $6,270,000 ($0.63 basic and fully diluted earnings per share), an increase of $789,000 or 14% from net income of $5,481,000 ($0.55 basic and fully diluted earnings per share, as adjusted for the stock dividend declared on November 14, 2025) for the quarter ended September 30, 2025.

Net interest income totaled $12,324,000 in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of $1,426,000 or 13% from the same period in 2025. This resulted primarily from an increase in the interest rate spread from 2.88% to 3.15%, and by an increase in excess of interest-earning assets over interest-bearing liabilities of $8.5 million. The increase in the interest rate spread is primarily attributable to an increase of 0.32% in yield on average interest-earning assets offset by an increase of 0.05% in rate paid on average interest-bearing liabilities.

Other operating income decreased $11,000 in the third quarter of 2026 to $207,000 from $218,000 for the same period in 2025.

Operating expenses increased 5% in the third quarter of 2026 to $3,616,000 from $3,445,000 in the third quarter of 2025. The increase is primarily attributed to an increase in data processing of $76,000 and compensation of $92,000.

The Company had no delinquent loans and no foreclosed real estate owned at September 30, 2026. The Company’s allowance for loan losses was $3,797,000, or 0.31% of total loans, at September 30, 2026.

Randy C. Bowers, Chairman, President and CEO, commented, “We are pleased to report record year-over-year earnings for both the third quarter and the first nine months of 2026. These positive earnings trends along with excellent asset quality and tight expense control position us well for favorable performance for the remainder of the year. Despite a highly competitive and volatile operating environment, we remain optimistic about our momentum and thank our entire team for their efforts in achieving these results.”

The Company’s total assets increased by 2% to $1.463 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.428 billion at September 30, 2025. The loan portfolio at September 30, 2026, was $1.237 billion, an increase of $24.9 million or 2% from September 30, 2025. The Company originates loans principally for its own portfolio and not for sale.

The Company funds its assets with a mix of retail deposits, wholesale deposits and FHLB borrowings. Retail deposits totaled $725.7 million as of September 30, 2026, a $2.2 million increase from $723.5 million at September 30, 2025. Wholesale deposits increased $20.5 million or 10% from $211.2 million at September 30, 2025, to $231.7 million at September 30, 2026. Wholesale deposits are primarily comprised of State of California certificates of deposit in the amount of $51.0 million, long-term institutional deposits of $9.4 million and $171.3 million of long-term brokered certificates of deposits. FHLB borrowings increased $5.0 million or 2% from $240.0 million at September 30, 2025, to $245.0 million at September 30, 2026. The Company utilizes long-term certificates of deposit (retail and wholesale) and FHLB borrowings to manage interest rate risk.

As of September 30, 2026, Malaga Bank was in compliance with all applicable regulatory capital requirements and was deemed “well-capitalized” under applicable regulations. Core capital and risk-based capital ratios were 16.85% and 28.09%, respectively, significantly exceeding the minimum “well-capitalized” requirements of 5% and 10%, respectively.

Malaga Bank, a subsidiary of Malaga Financial Corporation, is a full-service community bank headquartered on the Palos Verdes Peninsula with six offices located in the South Bay area of Los Angeles. For over fifteen years Malaga Bank has been consistently recommended by one of the nation’s leading independent bank rating and research firms, Bauer Financial Inc. Malaga Bank was awarded Bauer’s premier Top 5-Star rating for the 75th consecutive quarter as of June 2026. Since 1985 Malaga has been delivering competitive banking services to residents and businesses of South Bay, including real estate loan products custom-tailored to consumers and investors. As the largest community bank in the South Bay, Malaga is proud of its continuing tradition of relationship-based banking and legendary customer service. data.title: Katie Zacharia 'transitioning out' of her role as press secretary
data.description:
Current White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia is “transitioning out” of her role, according to a White House senior official.

The New York Times reported that Zacharia had been ousted on Friday, citing three people familiar with the matter. The White House was able to confirm with Seeking Alpha that Zacharia is leaving her post.

Zacharia has been under scrutiny due to how she presented her legal career and how she handled her press briefing. Her role as White House press secretary began on Oct. 12.

President Donald Trump was questioned by reporters outside the White House and said, “Maybe the role is not for her.” He mentioned that he told her she did not have to stay in her role.

“I’m going to let her make the decision,” he said. “If I were her, I’d reconsider.”

data.title: Nearly 12,000 California residents bought EVs using state rebate program
data.description:
By David Shepardson

California said on Friday nearly 12,000 residents bought electric vehicles using rebates under a new $270 million program funded by the state and automakers.

Still, overall EV sales have fallen both in California and nationwide as President Donald Trump's administration has removed federal incentives for EVs. EV sales are up globally.

The program for California residents buying their first EV was signed into law by Governor Gavin Newsom in July and offers $3,500 rebates on new EVs with retail prices of up to $50,000 and a $1,750 rebate for used EVs costing no more than $25,000.

California said EVs accounted for 18% of all state sales through September 30 compared to 23% last year and 25% in 2024. Tesla vehicles account for more than half of EVs sold in California.

The program is still offering rebates through participating automakers, including Ford , GM , Honda , Hyundai , Kia, Toyota and its Lexus brand, Lucid, Nissan , Rivian , Subaru <9778.T>, and Volvo.

There are no funds remaining for Tesla models under the program, which includes $135.5 million in state funding and $135.5 million from participating automakers.

The federal government has dropped support for EVs and charging programs. Trump signed legislation in 2025 that killed the federal $7,500 EV tax credit and the federal $4,000 used EV credit, which has reduced US sales.

California's previous rebate program ended in 2023 and spent $1.49 billion to subsidize 586,000 EV purchases ​over a decade.

Trump has taken aim at EVs on a number of fronts, including signing legislation in June 2025 against California's rules adopted by nearly a dozen other states that aim to phase out new gasoline-powered cars by 2035. California has sued ⁠to challenge ​the procedure used to reverse the landmark EV ​rules.

The administration has finalized other changes that will save automakers billions of dollars in purchasing credits from ​Tesla and others to meet prior regulatory requirements.

data.title: Wheat Futures Fall as Grains Limp Into Weekend — Daily Grain Highlights
data.description:
By Kirk Maltais

-Wheat for December delivery fell 1.5% to $6.59 3/4 a bushel on the Chicago Board of Trade Friday, with the overall grains complex finishing off the week under pressure amid tough macro conditions and friendlier-than-expected weather in the Corn Belt.

-Corn for December delivery fell 0.8% to $4.74 1/4 a bushel.

-Soybeans for November delivery fell 0.2% to 12.60 1/2 a bushel.

HIGHLIGHTS

On the Home Front: Grain futures have been trending lower this fall in part because of a change in how traders are viewing the weather in crop-growing regions around the world. "The weather story that helped fuel grain-market optimism is beginning to unravel," said Scott Mathews of BestWeather in a note. "Improving rainfall across the U.S. Plains, favorable early-season conditions in South America, and substantial speculative exposure could leave corn, soybeans, and wheat vulnerable to additional selling." For corn and soybeans, this ties to weather allowing farmers in their fields to harvest their crops, while for wheat it means being able to get into the fields to plant.

Cut and Run: There's speculation fund traders are pulling out of long positions in corn, said Charlie Sernatinger of Marex in a note. "[Corn is] down anticipating a weekend harvest prehedge tonight, more chart selling, and talk that macro funds are exiting commodities anticipating a U.S. recession," says Sernatinger. Last week's Commitments of Traders report from the CFTC showed a sizable decrease in long corn positions, with nearly 55,000 long contracts shown being closed. The CFTC will be updating its report this afternoon, although the data is a few days behind.

Feeling Flat: The USDA this week announced multiple export sales of U.S. soybeans to China, including a new flash sale of 558,000 tons announced today. An additional 236,000 tons of soybeans sold to "unknown destinations" were also reported. "Unknown destinations" is an alternative moniker that's often used for Chinese buyers, although not necessarily the case. But CBOT soybeans didn't respond by going higher, as China's return to buying U.S. soybeans was at least partially expected, said Joe Davis of Futures International in a note.

INSIGHT

Slack Showing: Grain futures closed out the week with a weak showing, continuing a skid that began last month. Corn settled lower for the fourth session in a row, according to FactSet data. Soybeans finished the week in the negative for the fifth session in a row, making it 7 out of the past 8 sessions it's closed down. Wheat finished lower for the 6th session out of the past 8. A stronger U.S. dollar and friendlier-than-expected weather in the Corn Belt has applied the pressure to the grains complex.

Farming for the Future: U.S. farmers are increasingly utilizing drones to spray their farmland, said the American Farm Bureau Federation in a note. The AFBF says that 16.4 million acres of farmland were sprayed by drones in 2025, up roughly five times from 3.7 million acres in 2023. The usage of drones is increasing as farmers see them as ways to handle problems with accessing certain portions of their fields. "The biggest advantages for drones come in wet fields, rough terrain, irregularly shaped fields and situations where timely product applications are critical," said Bernt Nelson of the AFBF.

AHEAD

-The USDA will release its weekly Grain Export Inspections report at 11 a.m. ET Monday.

-The USDA will release its weekly Crop Progress report at 4 p.m. ET Monday.

-The EIA will release its Weekly Petroleum Status Update report at 10:30 a.m. ET Wednesday.

data.title: Chino Commercial Bancorp Reports 22% Increase in Third Quarter Earnings
data.description:
CHINO, Calif., Oct. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The Board of Directors of Chino Commercial Bancorp , the parent company of Chino Commercial Bank, N.A., announced the results of operations for the Bank and the consolidated holding company for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Net earnings for the third quarter of 2026 were $1.88 million, reflecting an increase of $338 thousand, or an increase of 22%, compared to the same period last year. Basic and diluted earnings per share were $0.49 for the third quarter of 2026, up from $0.40 for the same quarter in 2025. Net earnings increased year-to-date by $951 thousand, or 21%, to $5.39 million, as compared to $4.43 million for the same period last year. Year-to-date basic and diluted earnings per share were $1.40 for the period ending September 30, 2026, as compared with $1.15 or a 22% increase over the same period last year. Earnings per share for the prior year were adjusted for the 20 percent stock dividend, which was payable to shareholders of record as of June 18, 2026.

Dann H. Bowman, President and Chief Executive Officer, stated “We are pleased with the Bank’s performance year-to-date and during the third quarter of 2026, which set new records for total Assets, total Deposits, total Loans, Net Earnings, and Capital. In addition, Loan quality remains very strong, with the Bank having no delinquent loans at quarter-end.

Locally, we believe the economic engine of the Inland Empire is strong and diverse, and the Bank is well positioned to continue to help the small business customers in our market.”

Financial Condition

As of September 30, 2026, total assets were $543 million, being an increase of $49 million, or 10%, over $494 million on December 31, 2025. Total deposits rose by $43.2 million, or 11.7%, to $413.4 million, up from $370.2 million on December 31, 2025. Core deposits accounted for 97.5% of total deposits as of September 30, 2026.

Gross loans increased by $32.6 million, or 14.8%, totaling $253.2 million as of September 30, 2026, compared to $220.6 million as of December 31, 2025. At the end of the third quarter, the Bank reported no delinquent loans and three nonaccrual loans totaling $1.2 million. As of September 30, 2026, the Bank had no Other Real Estate Owned (OREO) properties.

Earnings

The Company reported net interest income of $4.7 million for the three months ending September 30, 2026, compared to $4.0 million for the same period in 2025, an increase of $656.9 thousand. Average interest-earning assets were $443.2 million, while average interest-bearing liabilities totaled $234.4 million, resulting in a net interest margin of 4.20% for the third quarter of 2026. This compares favorably with the prior year’s third quarter margin of 3.78%, based on average interest-earning assets of $423.0 million and average interest-bearing liabilities of $223.3 million.

Non-interest income for the third quarter of 2026 was $924.9 thousand, which was an increase of 3.72% compared to $891.8 thousand for the same period last year. Much of the increase was from higher Merchant Service processing fees, which rose by $91 thousand or 44% to $297 thousand. These increases were partially offset by reductions in lower Service Charges and Fees of $87 thousand or 19%, due to lower overdraft and other deposit account related charges.

The Bank’s Merchant Services Program continues to be one of the Company's fastest-growing business lines. For the quarter ending September 30, 2026, card processing sales volume increased by $7.1 million or 40% to $24.9 million, compared with $17.8 million for the same quarter last year. On a year-to-date basis through September 30, 2026, card processing sales volume increased by $17.2 million or 39.1% to $61.0 million, as compared to $43.8 million for the same period last year.

General and administrative expenses totaled $2.8 million for the three months ending September 30, 2026, compared to $2.8 million for the same period in 2025. data.title: Eastman Chemical cut at J.P. Morgan as commodity spreads no longer favorable
data.description:
Eastman Chemical slipped 2.6% in Friday's trading as J.P. Morgan downgraded the specialty chemicals company to Neutral from Overweight with a $66 price target, lowered from $82, saying commodity spreads are no longer favorable as propane prices rise while propylene and ethylene prices fall.

The price of propane has climbed to $1.07/gal from $0.74 at the end of August, but the spot price of polymer-grade propylene has moved lower at $0.39/gal from $0.41, which took the propane-propylene spread to ~$0.02/lb from $0.11 in August, JPM analyst Jeffrey Zekauskas said, noting that Eastman produces ~500M lbs of propylene and buys 500M lbs on a cost-plus basis, and the narrowing of spreads could lower annual EBITDA by $90M.

Likewise, the price of ethylene has moved lower to $0.235/lb from $0.25 since the end of August, while the price of ethane rose to $0.31/gal from $0.24, cutting the ethylene spread to $0.05/lb from $0.10 at the end of August, which could shave $55M in annual EBITDA from August levels.

"We had thought that operating income from the Chemical Intermediates segment could be about $130M in 2026," Zekauskas wrote. "We think it could be close to break even in 2027."

data.title: House of the Week: An English Manor in Virginia Hunt Country — WSJ
data.description:
By Katherine Clarke

Candy and Greg Fazakerley were sitting at their kitchen table in Washington, D.C., one morning when Greg made a suggestion out of the blue: Perhaps they should buy a house in the country.

Candy, a horse lover who grew up in rural Virginia, was delighted by the idea. When the couple couldn't find something they loved, they decided to build something instead.

Around 1995, they paid close to $800,000 for more than 100 acres in Virginia Hunt Country. The couple, who worked in real-estate development, spent the next decade planning, designing and creating an English Baroque-inspired manor house built with Indiana limestone and Brazilian granite. They called it Wayside.

Greg says the home, which is located about 35 miles west of Fairfax, looks like it has been standing for centuries. When subcontractors asked when he started the renovation, he would gleefully respond that it was actually a new house.

"That is a very nice compliment," he says, "because that's what we were trying to accomplish."

The perfect spot

It took Candy, 80, four years after purchasing the land to decide on the perfect site for the house. Meanwhile, they lived in a smaller cabin on site and built the stables, where they kept two horses and a small pony for their grandchildren.

One day, while out on a long walk, Greg heard Candy shriek.

"She hops over the fence like a teenager, walks back into these woods, way ahead of me and all of a sudden she starts screaming. 'I found it!'" Greg, 78, says. "'I found where the house is going.'"

Designed by the classical architect Michael M. Franck, the house has a symmetrical facade with a Belgian block granite motor court and a limestone water feature out front.

Can't-miss features

The Fazakerelys traveled the world in search of fixtures and finishes for Wayside. The couple visited a quarry in Italy to hand-select Carrara marble for several of the fireplaces.

A grand central hall with 12-foot ceilings has broad slabs of Jerusalem gold marble, while a library has carved walnut paneling.

Reasons for selling?

Greg says they want to spend more time in California, where their children and grandchildren are based.

What they'll miss?

Living in nature. "Candy has wonderfully exposed me to the countryside, the deer and rabbits," Greg says.

What they won't miss?

Pulling out the tractor after a big snowfall to clear the road that leads in and out of the property.

Market snapshot

Listing agent Daniel Heider of Sotheby's International Realty says there have been a string of big-ticket sales in Virginia horse country over the past year. Cisco Systems co-founder Sandy Lerner sold her historic Virginia estate, Ayrshire Farm, for $19.8 million in February. A nearby estate known as Llangollen sold around the same time for $21.35 million.

data.title: Antofagasta nets its best ever copper treatment charges in auction, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Concentrate shortages have been building since 2023
  • Deficit also due to massive rise in China's smelting capacity
  • Concentrate supply contract talks for 2027 set to begin

By Pratima Desai and Tom Daly

Chile's Antofagasta was paid more than $300 a metric ton to have its copper concentrate turned into metal in recent tenders, two sources familiar with the matter said, underscoring acute supply shortages as contract talks for 2027 begin.

One of the sources said the numbers represent a record result for Antofagasta, while the second person and a third market source said Canada's Teck Resources sold material from its Highland Valley mine for treatment charges in the minus $370s a few weeks ago.

Shortages have been building due to a series of disruptions starting with First Quantum's Cobre Panama mine, which was shut in late 2023, and most recently a landslide at Codelco's El Teniente mine in Chile that left two workers dead.

Miners historically paid treatment and refining charges (TC/RCs) to process their concentrate into refined copper, offset against the cost of the copper contained in the ore.

But at the start of last year treatment charges turned negative, which essentially means smelters reliant on feedstock from miners — mostly in China — are paying to keep their operations running.

In one recent tender, Antofagasta secured a negative treatment charge of $310 a ton for 10,000 tons of concentrate — partially processed copper ore — from its Centinela mine for November shipment, the sources said, declining to be identified.

In another auction, it sold 40,000 tons from Los Pelambres spread over next year in the minus $330s.

Antofagasta and Teck declined to comment.

MATING SEASON UNDER WAY

The low numbers come as Antofagasta prepares to begin talks with smelters for copper concentrate supply next year on the sidelines of the London Metal Exchange Week gathering in London.

The first TC/RC settlement between a major miner — which in recent years has been Antofagasta — and a smelter from China, the world's biggest copper consumer, traditionally serves as a benchmark for annual supply contracts.

Concentrate shortages are in part due to a massive build-out of smelting capacity in China, which now produces over half of global supplies of refined copper, crucial for electric vehicles, power grids, construction and military equipment.

China's copper smelting capacity, estimated at 13 million to 14 million tons this year, has increased more than 70% over the last decade.

Chinese smelters continue to buy at negative TC/RCs on the spot market, managing to break even thanks to copper prices near record highs, and their sales of byproducts sulphuric acid — prices of which have shot up due to the conflict in the Middle East — and gold.

data.title: Soybeans hit seven-week low, corn down on dry Midwest harvest weather outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • Drier forecast should speed Midwest fieldwork and Plains winter sowing
  • USDA confirms 558,000 metric tons of US soybeans sold to China on Friday
  • Black Sea shipping attacks failed to offset broader pressure from technical selling and fund exits

By Karl Plume

US soybean futures dropped to a seven-week low on Friday while corn futures neared a two-month low as dry Midwest weather expected over the coming week was likely to fuel rapid harvesting progress.

Wheat futures slid to a two-month low, posting a seventh straight weekly drop, as favorable winter crop planting weather in the Plains pressured prices.

Technical selling and long liquidation ahead of the weekend pressured crop markets despite field work delays in many areas this week due to widespread rains.

"Rain should linger in the northeastern Midwest and far southern Plains today, but drier weather is expected in all areas this weekend and early next week. This will favor corn and soybean harvesting as well as winter wheat planting," meteorologists with Vaisala said in a note.

Chicago Board of Trade November soybeans (SX26) ended down 1-3/4 cents at $12.61-1/4 a bushel after earlier sinking to the lowest point since August 27. The benchmark contract posted a 2.4% weekly drop despite renewed demand from top importer China.

The US Department of Agriculture on Friday confirmed private sales totalling 558,000 metric tons of US soybeans to China, bringing the confirmed sales total to China to 1.358 million tons over the past three days.

December corn (CZ26) fell 3-3/4 cents to $4.74-1/4 a bushel after dropping to within 3 cents of a two-month low posted last week when the USDA unexpectedly raised its US harvest forecast. The contract was down 1.1% for the week, a third straight weekly decline.

CBOT December wheat (WZ26) slid to $6.60-1/2 a bushel, down 9-1/2 cents on the day. The contract fell 1.6% in the week and has not posted a weekly gain since late August despite concerns about Russian and Ukrainian supplies amid continued attacks on ships in the Black Sea.

data.title: Why Fox Can Finally Breathe a Sigh of Relief With the Roku Deal-and Why the NFL Can't — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Kit Norton

Fox Corp.'s $22 billion acquisition of Roku will enhance how the media titan delivers its programming directly to viewers, a huge plus for livestreaming — especially its Sunday NFL games.

The deal, approved by Fox and Roku shareholders this week and expected to close early next year, essentially takes the risk off the table that the NFL will renew its 10-year contract with Fox early. The contract runs through 2033, but has an opt-out clause that either party can exercise after the 2029 season.

An early renewal has weighed on Wall Street — billions spent on traditional TV, the NFL's right to move high-profile games to powerful platforms like Amazon, and NFL's massive media rights that just keep going up.

And all of these things without new ways for Fox to make money.

Nailing down the deal, though, has analysts singing a different tune because of Roku's streaming operating system on TVs and revenue from ads and subscription fees for other streamer such as Netflix and Comcast's Peacock.

On Friday, Bank of America's Jessica Reif Ehrlich double upgraded Fox to Buy from Underperform and raised her price target to $85 from $54. The change sent shares 0.2% higher to $64.11 on Friday.

"One billion reasons to love the Roku deal," Ehrlich wrote, adding that the acquisition "changes the equation" for Fox stock.

Ehrlich said the early renewal risk and Fox's long-term positioning in streaming were behind her Underperform rating.

"With the risk of a near term NFL renewal largely receding until the 2029 opt-out window, the Roku acquisition fundamentally changes the strategic and financial narrative," she said.

Roku provides Fox with a credible path to transition toward a direct-to-consumer model, which has been a weakness for the company, Ehrlich said.

It also adds to Fox's current direct-to-consumer product, FOX One.

"One of the core bear arguments on Fox has been that the company...lacked a robust direct-to-consumer strategy to fully capture the migration of audiences and advertising budgets away from traditional pay-TV," she said. "Roku addresses this existential question," she added.

On Wall Street, Fox has an average Buy rating with a price target of $77.75, according to FactSet. The stock has six Buy ratings, seven Hold ratings, and one Sell rating.

Fox and Barron's parent News Corp share common ownership.

data.title: US arms firm Anduril could make interceptors in Europe, executive says
data.description:
US defence firm Anduril could eventually manufacture its newly unveiled Steelfin interceptor missiles in Europe, a company executive said this week, as governments aim to expand air-defence production after global conflicts highlighted shortages of interceptor missiles.

"I certainly hope that something like Steelfin could become a capability that we engage with both the Polish customer and industry," Brian Moran, Anduril's vice president for Europe, told Reuters on Monday.

"We would definitely consider engaging European partners and customers on this capability." Steelfin is due to undergo flight testing in 2027, according to Anduril.

Wars in Ukraine and the Gulf have strained stocks of air-defence interceptor missiles and caused delivery delays.

Moran said Anduril saw Steelfin as a complementary system that could provide a more affordable interceptor alongside existing missile-defence systems like the Patriot and others.

The company is already in talks to establish production in Poland of its Barracuda-500 cruise missile, and Moran said that experience could open the door to additional manufacturing projects.

"We're having a very good experience with our industry partner here, PGZ," he said, adding that discussions were also under way with the defence ministry and other government agencies. PGZ is Poland's state-owned arms group.

Poland, one of NATO's top defence spenders relative to the size of its economy, is seeking to expand domestic arms production and reduce reliance on foreign suppliers.

Moran said talks with PGZ, its WZL-2 unit and the government were focused on balancing local production with delivery speed and Poland's specific military requirements.

Asked about growing calls in Europe for defence-industrial sovereignty, Moran said the term could mean different things, from security of supply and maintenance capabilities to control over software upgrades and future modifications.

"Sovereignty has a cost. There's a cost to localisation. There's cost in terms of timing and just schedule. And those need to be considered in light of the threats that Europe collectively is facing."

While governments also want economic benefits from defence spending, the military outcome is most important, he said, adding that greater localisation can come with additional costs and longer timelines.

data.title: Dollar heads for weekly loss as Fed hike bets fade, AI jitters linger
data.description:
Key points:
  • Dollar set for first weekly loss after a month of gains
  • Investors scale back Fed hike bets despite hot inflation data
  • Tech selloff also weighing on dollar

By Laura Matthews

The dollar was lower on Friday and on track for its first weekly fall in more than a month against the euro and the yen, reflecting fading expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike and lingering concerns about an AI-driven equity selloff.

Hotter-than-expected consumer and producer price readings initially rattled markets this week, but comments from Fed officials signaling no urgency to tighten policy further helped stabilize Treasury yields and eroded support for the dollar.

AI stocks fell sharply this week and the stress spread to parts of the credit market as investors who have crowded into bets all along the supply chain worry data centre operators might not manage to be profitable in time to pay their debts.

"What I found most interesting today and more broadly this week, is how closely the dollar has been tied to the AI trade," said Matt Weller, global head of market research at StoneX in Michigan. "Usually if we see a sell off in tech stocks you would expect the greenback to get a safe-haven bid. We are seeing an element of that into bonds, but the dollar is actually falling."

The dollar index , which measures it against six major peers, fell 0.17% to 101.87 and was set for a 0.35% weekly drop.

The pound and the Swiss franc led gains against the dollar this week, with the latter buoyed by safe-haven demand and expectations that even in a lower-rates environment Switzerland is unlikely to cut policy rates below the current zero level.

Sterling rose 0.31% to $1.3314 and was up 0.63% on the week, while the dollar fell 0.25% against the Swiss franc to 0.8246, leaving it down 0.67% for the week. The franc has gained more than 1.4% in the last two sessions.

Markets assign an 83% probability to the Fed keeping rates unchanged later this month, up from 49% a month earlier, the CME FedWatch Tool shows.

At the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh offered no clues about future rate decisions, saying he does not "prejudge meetings."

"I don’t think there is enough support in (the) committee, particularly from the governors, for a rate hike in October. It still leaves December an unanswered question and there is a lot to happen between now and then," said John Velis, Americas macro strategist at BNY in New York.

EURO AREA FISCAL RISKS STILL IN FOCUS

Fiscal risks in France remained in the background after the jump in the French debt risk premium in early October.

The euro was last up 0.08% to $1.1227 after climbing 0.56% on Thursday in its biggest daily rise in two months, putting it on track for a 0.23% weekly gain.

Investors expect US President Donald Trump to steer clear of any escalation in the Middle East or Ukraine, as a broader conflict could hurt his standing ahead of midterm elections by fuelling inflation.

Against the yen the dollar slipped 0.08% to 158.11, leaving the Japanese currency on track for a 0.13% weekly rise after dropping for four consecutive weeks as the Iran conflict supported the greenback.

Higher oil prices recently have been boosting the dollar while weighing on the currencies of energy-importing countries, such as those tied to the euro and yen.

BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda on Friday reiterated the risks of underlying inflation overshooting the central bank's 2% target.
